links.outcome: Agreement of AI vs visual ANA positive/negative classification on local consecutive clinical samples
links.effect: At cut-off 80, kappa 0.69 but significantly different (McNemar p<0.0001); at cut-off ≥1/80 kappa 0.76 and no significant difference (p=1.0000). Pattern agreement moderate (kappa 0.54).
links.quote: Agreement of positive/negative ANA discrimination between AI-aided and VI-IIFT at the recommended cut-off of 80 was good (Cohen's kappa [κ] 0.69) but significantly different (McNemar test, p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: AI titer levels versus gold standard visual interpretation, indicating miscalibrated thresholds
links.effect: Titer levels in automated evaluations were frequently assessed at higher values than visual interpretation; agreement improved when cut-off was adjusted to ≥1/80 (kappa 0.69 to 0.76).
links.quote: Notably, titer levels in the automated evaluations were frequently assessed at higher values than in the gold standard interpretation.

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and concordance of an AI-based indirect immunofluorescence automated interpretation system (akiron NEO) against visual interpretation on clinical serum samples, but does not test a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
